version_history.change: Initial 7-check gate: SED, stress_law, compressibility_formulation, parameter_mapping, stress_measure, quadrature, reference_configuration

Added 8th check: tangent_equivalence. Per CEO Round 84 directive: 'Two solvers can produce similar stresses at one deformation state while having different tangents, which can produce different Newton paths and failure behavior. The gate should therefore compare: energy -> stress -> tangent, not just energy -> stress.'

gate_rule.name: Constitutive-Equivalence Hard Gate (v1.1.0)
gate_rule.formula: L3_permitted = (sed_equivalent AND stress_equivalent AND tangent_equivalent AND compressibility_equivalent AND parameter_mapping_equivalent AND stress_measure_equivalent AND quadrature_equivalent AND reference_configuration_equivalent)
gate_rule.shortcut_refusal: If material_label_same = true BUT any of the eight equivalence checks above = false, L3 is REFUSED. The material label is NOT evidence of constitutive equivalence.
shortcut_refusal_examples: FEBio 'neo-Hookean' uses W_vol = (K/2)(ln J)^2; SfePy 'dw_tl_bulk_penalty' uses W_vol = (K/2)(J-1)^2. Both labeled 'neo-Hookean', but volumetric SED differs. REFUSED on check #1 (sed_equivalent).

Solver A uses a numerical Jacobian (finite differences) while Solver B uses an analytical Jacobian. Stresses may agree but tangents differ at finite perturbation. REFUSED on check #3 (tangent_equivalent).

FEBio outputs Cauchy stress; SfePy 'term_mode=stress' outputs 2nd Piola-Kirchhoff stress. Same model, different stress measure. REFUSED on check #5 (stress_measure) until both pushed forward / pulled back to same measure.

1_strain_energy_density.description: Both solvers must use the SAME mathematical form of W(C, J). The functional form (including all invariants, exponents, and dependencies) must be identical, not just 'similar'.
1_strain_energy_density.audit_method: Write down the actual W function from each solver's source/manual, side by side. Check character-by-character equivalence of the mathematical expression.
common_violations: (K/2)(ln J)^2 vs (K/2)(J-1)^2  — logarithmic vs quadratic volumetric penalty
Mooney-Rivlin W = C1(I1-3) + C2(I2-3) vs neo-Hookean W = (mu/2)(I1-3)  — different terms even if 'similar'
Ogden W = sum_i (mu_i/alpha_i)(lambda_1^alpha_i + lambda_2^alpha_i + lambda_3^alpha_i - 3) vs neo-Hookean  — different functional form

2_stress_law.description: Both solvers must derive stress from W via the SAME formula. For hyperelasticity, S = 2 dW/dC is standard, but variations exist.
2_stress_law.audit_method: Compare the stress formula in each solver's documentation/source. Verify S_dev and S_vol expressions match exactly.
common_violations: S = 2 dW/dC (standard) vs S = dW/dE (where E = (C-I)/2; equivalent if consistent, but watch for missing factors)
Deviatoric-volumetric split (S = S_dev + S_vol) vs single-form S — must be algebraically equivalent

3_tangent_equivalence.description: Both solvers must produce the SAME tangent modulus (dσ/dε or equivalently dσ/dλ) at multiple deformation states. The tangent is the derivative of stress with respect to strain. Two solvers can produce identical stresses at one state but different tangents, which leads to different Newton paths and different convergence behavior.
3_tangent_equivalence.audit_method: Evaluate the analytical tangent d(σ_zz)/d(λ_z) at 5 deformation states spanning the benchmark range (e.g., λ_z = 1.000, 1.025, 1.050, 1.075, 1.100). Compare against each solver's material tangent. Relative difference must be < 1% at all 5 states.
3_tangent_equivalence.tolerance_rationale: Tangent should match to machine precision for an exact constitutive replication. 1% allows for finite-difference noise in numerical tangents. Tighter than the 5% stress tolerance because tangent errors compound through Newton iterations.
3_tangent_equivalence.material_tangent_vs_solver_tangent: This check applies to the MATERIAL TANGENT (dσ/dε computed analytically from the constitutive law), NOT the SOLVER TANGENT (the matrix used in Newton iterations). FEBio's BFGS quasi-Newton uses a secant approximation that is NOT the true tangent — this is fine for solving, but the constitutive equivalence check must use the material tangent, not BFGS.
common_violations: Solver uses a numerical Jacobian with too-large finite-difference step — produces correct stress but wrong slope
Solver uses a different tangent formulation (material vs consistent)
Solver has a bug in the tangent implementation (correct stress, wrong slope)
Solver uses a quasi-Newton approximation (BFGS) that has not yet converged — not a constitutive issue, but the material tangent should still be available for verification

4_compressibility_formulation.description: For compressible materials, both solvers must use the SAME volumetric law. This is where 'neo-Hookean' labels diverge most often.
4_compressibility_formulation.audit_method: Identify the volumetric term in each solver's W. Compare formulas directly. Note that 'mixed u-p formulation' (e.g., SfePy's dw_tl_bulk_pressure) is NOT automatically equivalent to a 'penalty formulation' (e.g., SfePy's dw_tl_bulk_penalty) — the equivalence must be proven mathematically.
common_violations: Pure displacement formulation with penalty (K/2)(J-1)^2
Mixed u-p formulation with (K/2)(ln J)^2 — SfePy dw_tl_bulk_pressure uses this
Sussman-Bathe mixed formulation
Three-field (F-bar) formulation
4_compressibility_formulation.mixed_formulation_warning: If solver A uses penalty and solver B uses mixed u-p, they may produce the SAME stress at convergence (when the pressure field has converged), but the formulations are mathematically distinct. The gate requires proof of equivalence, not just 'both labeled neo-Hookean'.

5_parameter_mapping.description: If the solvers accept different input parameters (E, nu vs mu, K vs C1, C2), the mapping must be exact and documented.
5_parameter_mapping.audit_method: Write down each solver's input parameters. Compute the mapping. Verify by substitution.
common_violations: E = 2mu(1+nu) vs E = 3mu(1-2nu) — first is correct, second is for pure shear, different physical regime
K = E/(3(1-2nu)) vs K = E/(2(1+nu)) — second is actually mu, not K
Ogden parameters mu_i, alpha_i vs Mooney-Rivlin C1, C2 — mapping is non-trivial

6_stress_measure.description: Both solvers must output stress in the SAME measure (Cauchy, 2nd PK, 1st PK, etc.). If different, the push-forward / pull-back transformation must be explicitly applied and verified.
6_stress_measure.audit_method: Identify the stress measure each solver outputs. If different, derive and apply the transformation.
common_violations: FEBio VTK 'stress' = Cauchy; SfePy 'term_mode=stress' = 2nd PK  — must push SfePy forward
Some FEBio materials output Kirchhoff stress tau = J*sigma  — must divide by J
Engineering strain vs Green strain  — different conjugate stress measures

7_quadrature.description: Both solvers must use the SAME numerical integration rule. For hex8, this is typically 2x2x2 Gauss (8 points) but other options exist.
7_quadrature.audit_method: Check each solver's integration order setting for the same element type.
common_violations: Full 2x2x2 Gauss vs reduced 1-point integration  — different locking behavior
Selectively reduced integration (B-bar method) vs uniform integration
Different Gauss point locations (Legendre vs Chebyshev)

8_reference_configuration.description: Both solvers must use the SAME reference configuration. For Total Lagrangian (TL), this is the undeformed geometry. For Updated Lagrangian (UL), this is the current deformed geometry.
8_reference_configuration.audit_method: Identify the formulation type for each solver. TL and UL are mathematically equivalent but require different bookkeeping.
common_violations: TL formulation integrating over Omega_0 vs UL formulation integrating over Omega_t  — equivalent if implemented correctly, but if outputs are taken at different times/steps, comparison is invalid
Reference temperature for thermal expansion  — must match

gate_enforcement.audit_frequency: Before every L3 cross-solver comparison attempt
gate_enforcement.audit_artifact_required: Each L3 attempt must include a CE-GATE-001-AUDIT-<solverA>-vs-<solverB>.json file alongside the L3 result. The audit must explicitly answer all 8 checks. If any check is 'false' or 'unknown', L3 is REFUSED.
gate_enforcement.refusal_action: If gate refuses L3, the orchestrator must NOT proceed with cross-solver comparison. Either (a) reconfigure one solver to match the other, OR (b) implement exact constitutive replication via custom term, OR (c) re-freeze a new benchmark version with a formulation both solvers natively implement.

sfepy_audit.3_tangent_equivalence: MUST be verified against L3-BENCHMARK-003-TANGENT-VERIFICATION.json at 5 states. Not yet checked for SfePy's automatic tangent.

applied_to_L3-BENCHMARK-002.febio_audit_PENDING: FEBio binary was wiped between sessions. When rebuilt, audit must be completed BEFORE any L3 run. Key risk: FEBio's default 'neo-Hookean' material uses (K/2)(ln J)^2 volumetric SED, which FAILS check #1 against this benchmark.

applied_to_L3-BENCHMARK-003.sfepy_audit: Same as B002 (B003 uses identical setup)
applied_to_L3-BENCHMARK-003.sfepy_calibration_status: SfePy numerical sigma_zz = 0.0961 vs analytical 0.096067 (0.034% diff) — calibration PASS at the stress level. Tangent check #3 not yet performed for SfePy's automatic tangent.

lessons_encoded: CE-020: Material label 'neo-Hookean' is NOT evidence of constitutive equivalence. FEBio uses (K/2)(ln J)^2 volumetric; SfePy uses (K/2)(J-1)^2. Encoded in v1.0.0 of this gate.

CE-021: Stress equivalence at one deformation state is NOT evidence of tangent equivalence. Two solvers can produce identical stresses but different tangents, leading to different Newton paths. Encoded in v1.1.0 of this gate (check #3 added).

CE-022: Mixed u-p formulation (e.g., SfePy dw_tl_bulk_pressure) is NOT automatically equivalent to penalty formulation (e.g., dw_tl_bulk_penalty) just because both can be labeled 'neo-Hookean'. The equivalence must be proven mathematically, not assumed.
